Les coulisses d’un salon de l’immobilier: Inside a real estate fair offering properties on Palestinian land
La plus vieille synagogue du Canada a-t-: Did Canada’s oldest synagogue really host a fair selling illegal properties?
Dans une salle de la Synagogue espagnole: In a room at Montréal’s Spanish and Portuguese Synagogue, the real estate fair’s booths welcome attendees. Photo: Loubna Chlaikhy
L’organisation d’un salon de l’immobilie: The organizing of an Israeli real estate fair, where properties located in illegally occupied territory in the West Bank were put up for sale, sparked outrage among part of the Jewish community and among all those who support Palestine. La Converse went. A demonstration called by Independent Jewish Voices Canada drew nearly 200 people in front of the Spanish and Portuguese Synagogue on Tuesday, March 5, 2024.
« Sionistes, rentrez chez vous, la Pales: “Zionists, go home, Palestine is not your home.” As night falls, a crowd protests the <l1>Israeli Real Estate Event</l1>, organized by the American group Keller Williams and its Israeli subsidiary Home in Israel. Kippas and Palestinian keffiyehs gather together under Palestinian flags flapping in the wind. Together, they denounce the holding of this event, at which properties located in illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank are offered for sale. More than 490,000 people currently live there.
« On a d’abord fait une campagne de publ: “We first ran a mailing campaign asking the synagogue to cancel this event, because selling stolen land is not a Jewish event, or a religious one, or a cultural one. We learned that after thinking about cancelling it, they decided to hold it anyway. So we called on the Jewish community and our Palestinian brothers and sisters to come together. It’s a very emotional evening for us, because it’s hard to protest in front of a synagogue, but it’s a message of love and justice that comes from our Jewish traditions,” says Sarah Boivin, a representative of <l1>Independent Jewish Voices</l1> (IJV) in Montréal.
À la suite des attaques menées par le Ha: Following the attacks carried out by Hamas on October 7, 2023, which killed at least 1,200 people according to the Hebrew state, Israeli reprisals have so far killed more than 30,200 people in Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. At the same time, Netanyahu’s government is promoting Aliyah, or the “return to the Land of Israel of the international Jewish diaspora” (a ministry is devoted to it), particularly among North American Jews.
C’est dans ce contexte qu’une tournée de: It is in this context that an Israeli real estate tour is being held for the first time in Montréal, as well as in Toronto and several U.S. cities this month. On the event’s website, the list of cities where properties are offered for sale stands out. Indeed, it includes several localities located in Israeli settlements in the West Bank, which are considered illegal under international law: Neve Daniel, Efrat and Ma’aleh Adumim.
« De tels transferts constituent un crim: “Such transfers constitute a war crime and may engage the individual criminal responsibility of those involved,” states a recent report by the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. For its part, Canada reaffirmed its position on November 20, 2023: “As successive Canadian governments have done, Canada does not recognize permanent Israeli control over the territories occupied since 1967, and strongly opposes <l1>illegal settlements</l1> in the West Bank.”
Alors, la plus vieille synagogue du Cana: So did Canada’s oldest synagogue really host a fair selling illegal properties? To try to understand the mindset of the participants at this real estate fair, La Converse went to the site.
« Est-ce que vous êtes juive ? » La ques: “Are you Jewish?” The question was put to one of my colleagues when she arrived at the entrance of the Montréal synagogue to cover the fair as a journalist. Her answer, no, was met with a flat refusal to let her in. Like her, several people who had registered to attend the event were unable to get past the security cordon set up by the police, at the edge of which an event agent was tasked with screening entrants. Yet buying property is not reserved for people of the Jewish faith, since Israeli law allows foreigners to settle or invest there.
Finalement, je parviens à entrer, prétex: In the end, I manage to get in, pretending to be looking for information on behalf of a fictitious father planning to buy in Israel. Inside, under the imposing chandelier of the synagogue’s main hall, a real estate fair is indeed under way, with booths and advertising banners.
Dès le premier kiosque, on m’encourage à: At the very first booth, I’m encouraged to move to Israel. “Many Jews have been coming to live in the Holy Land since October 7, you have to come. Come on vacation and you won’t want to leave, it’s your home!” a developer assures me.
Un peu plus loin, à un autre kiosque, un: A little further on, at another booth, a woman presents me with several real estate projects, including a particularly luxurious one in Efrat, an illegal settlement in the West Bank. “Look online, you’ll see it’s really beautiful. The community there is great, and it’s cheaper than in Israel,” she says, making no attempt to hide it. Foreigners are also exempt from tax on a purchase in Efrat. A way of saving money while extending the Israeli presence in the West Bank.
Le conflit actuel ne semble nullement pe: The current conflict seems to have no bearing at all on the real estate market, according to an exhibitor to whom I voice my concerns about the current situation in the Middle East. “We have more demand than supply, the market just keeps going up, it’s a guaranteed investment,” the developer assures me. “Don’t worry about the situation! The only problem with the Palestinians is that we no longer have them to work on the construction sites. But we’re bringing in Chinese workers to replace them.”
Ici, judaïsme, sionisme et immobilier ne: Here, Judaism, Zionism and real estate are one and the same. The real estate business has everything to gain, since these settlements, deemed illegal by the international community, are recognized by Israel. The construction of 3,426 housing units has just been approved by an Israeli body in the settlements of Ma’aleh Adumim, Kedar and Efrat in the West Bank. One more market for the sector, and one more example of the Hebrew state’s strategy.
Durant la soirée, trois membres des Voix: During the evening, three members of Independent Jewish Voices manage to get in. After a few moments, they shout their opposition. “Shame on you, I’m Jewish and you shame us! It’s illegal and shameful!” one of them yells, and is immediately removed by security to applause.
Interrogée sur la préparation de ces int: Asked about how these intrusions were prepared, Sarah Boivin says they were individual initiatives, which she welcomes. “It shows how desperate the members of Independent Jewish Voices are. These are very courageous actions to make our voice heard and to ask our religious authorities to make a decision of integrity and stop supporting a genocidal regime,” she says.
Mais l’effet escompté est loin d’être ob: But the intended effect is far from achieved, and many find the interruptions amusing. “It’s not illegal, it’s our home!” an exhibitor shouts. “Poor things, don’t they understand that we couldn’t care less about them outside?” a Keter Advisor real estate agent says mockingly.
Des exposants improvisent ensuite une co: Some exhibitors then improvise a counter-demonstration, Israeli flags in hand. “Israel is alive,” they sing in chorus.
« C’est chez nous, les colonies ! C’est: “The settlements are our home! You’re the ones who say it’s illegal, we say it’s Israel,” says Gabriel, a 28-year-old Montrealer. “They say they’re Jewish, but you can’t be Jewish and be against Israel,” says Sarah (not her real name).
À quelques mètres de distance, face à fa: A few metres apart, face to face, separated by a line of police officers, two visions of the same religion clash. “We’re living a moment that’s very representative of what the Jewish community is: a very close-knit community, but one with major divergences, political ones in particular. Anti-Zionist Jews have existed for as long as Zionism has, but our minority is growing. Our generation has learned that not only can we, but we must reject Zionism to be in line with our religious principles,” says Sarah Boivin. “We’re not protesting against the synagogue, but against this completely illegal real estate fair,” a protester is keen to stress.
Sarah Boivin, représentante des Voix Jui: Sarah Boivin, representative of Independent Jewish Voices, took the floor to thank the demonstrators for coming out to oppose the event.
Jeudi, les Voix Juives Indépendantes ont: On Thursday, Independent Jewish Voices learned that a temporary injunction from the Superior Court, dated Tuesday, March 5, targets them. It prohibits the organization, as well as several pro-Palestinian organizations, from demonstrating within 50 metres of 6 Jewish community institutions in Montréal.
D’un autre côté, aucune mesure n’a été p: On the other hand, no measures have been taken against the organizers of this North American tour promoting Israeli real estate, whether legal or not. On March 7, the tour stopped in Toronto, again in a synagogue. Independent Jewish Voices is surprised by the silence of Quebec and Canadian authorities and is calling for strong decisions to ban these illegal sales, considered by the United Nations to be “war crimes.”
Malgré plusieurs tentatives, nous n’avon: Despite several attempts, we received no response from representatives of the Spanish and Portuguese Synagogue or from the fair’s organizers. I went back to the site. Calm had returned to the place of worship, which I found closed on this day of the Sabbath, the day of rest for the Jewish community.
